culturalStory.heading: About the Silver Fox
body: The carved plaque reads sôniyâwâhkêsis — 'silver little-fox', the everyday Plains Cree way to name the rare silver-coated colour-phase of the red fox. sôniyâw is the same word for 'money', so the compound carries a soft double-reading: a 'money-fox', the kind of fox whose pelt was once worth a small fortune in the fur trade. The diminutive ‑âhkêsis is the bound, vowel-reduced version of the free NA noun mahkêsîs 'fox'.

The plaque art picks up the same poise — a stylized white-and-black silhouette of a fox in a flowing, kitsune-like pose, head turned and tail curling forward. The carving is mostly black on white with red syllabics. The English label is rendered as SILVEREFOX on this particular plaque (extra E between SILVER and FOX) — likely a layout/carving quirk; the catalogue and most signage use the more standard Silverfox.

Silver Fox the trail is a short descent in the Kinsmen / Emily Murphy network in Northwest Edmonton, ridden as part of the popular 'Shredders Kinsmen Loop' alongside nikocwâsaskanôs / Six Shooter and sâpwâpahcikan pâskisikan / Ray Gun. It sits on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory).

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE: The current catalogue creeSyllabics for soniyawahkesis is ᓲᓂᔮᐁᐦᑫᓯᐢ — the fourth glyph ᐁ ('e') appears to be a transcription error. The SRO sôniyâwâhkêsis breaks into syllables sô‑ni‑yâ‑wâ‑h‑kê‑sis, which yields ᓲᓂᔮᐚᐦᑫᓯᐢ with ᐚ ('wâ') as the fourth glyph. Coordinator should update catalogue.json creeSyllabics 'ᓲᓂᔮᐁᐦᑫᓯᐢ' → 'ᓲᓂᔮᐚᐦᑫᓯᐢ' (ᐁ → ᐚ).

The plaque's English text appears to read 'SILVEREFOX' (one word, extra E inserted between SILVER and FOX) rather than 'SILVERFOX'. This may be a carving / layout artefact (the letters were arranged to fill the plaque) or an intentional stylization. Flagged for user review — the catalogue.json englishName 'Silverfox' is the conventional form and is left unchanged.

Folder path on disk includes diacritics: 'sôniyâwâhkêsîs' (with all three circumflexes plus a long î at the very end). The folder name uses 'sîs' (long î) at the end, but the SRO carved on the plaque uses 'sis' (short i) — this short-i form is the standard Plains Cree spelling (matches Wolvengrey). Coordinator should leave the folder path unchanged (legacy), and the on-page SRO uses the standard short-i form.
